name: Six Street Qualities in Shanghai: Pairwise
description:
Method replication: participants compare pairs of Shanghai street views in six parts of 8 pairs, with the paper's questions and definitions: Which place looks greener / more walkable / safer? Which place has better imageability / enclosure / complexity? The images are not the paper's stimuli (64 Baidu Street View images sampled across Shanghai from the centre to the outskirts, 2017–2023, fetched for this template).
Original study: Qiu, Li, Liu, Zhang, Li & Huang (2023), "Subjective and objective measures of streetscape perceptions: Relationships with property value in Shanghai", Cities 132, 104037. 43 designers (architecture, city planning, landscape architecture) who had lived in Shanghai made 4,426 pairwise choices on 300 randomly sampled Baidu street views (heading along the street, 120° field of view, pitch 0°). TrueSkill scores trained models that predicted the six qualities across Shanghai, and these subjective measures were compared with segmentation-based objective measures in hedonic house price models.
Differences from the original study: (1) 64 new Baidu images instead of the paper's 300; our random sample includes many suburban and rural roads; (2) images are cropped to about a 100° field of view to remove the capture car; (3) 48 pairs per participant (8 per quality) instead of about 100; (4) open to anyone, with questions on field and whether the participant has lived in Shanghai.
author: Qiu, Li, Liu, Zhang, Li & Huang

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: greenness
elements.title: Which place looks greener?
elements.description: Greenness: urban green space including forests, greenbelts and lawns.

elements.name: walkability
elements.title: Which place looks more walkable?
elements.description: Walkability: the psychological impact of the surrounding visual elements (e.g. comfort and pleasure) on the walking experience.

elements.name: safety
elements.title: Which place looks safer?
elements.description: Safety: an individual’s experience of the risk of becoming a victim of crime and disturbance of public order.

elements.name: imageability
elements.title: Which place has better imageability?
elements.description: Imageability: the quality of a place that makes it distinct, recognizable and memorable.

elements.name: enclosure
elements.title: Which place has better enclosure?
elements.description: Enclosure: the degree to which streets and other public spaces are visually defined by buildings, walls, trees and other vertical elements.

elements.name: complexity
elements.title: Which place has better complexity?
elements.description: Complexity: numbers and types of buildings, ornamentation, landscape elements, street furniture, signage and human activity.
